title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, tool calling, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Anya Patel
title_short: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming + tool calls + formatting
description: Context: We aim for parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions API for Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR addresses several gaps discovered during customer testing and internal evals: streaming stability improvements for multi-chunk responses, deterministic role handling (system/user/assistant), support for stop tokens and logprobs in non-streaming and streaming paths, and response formatting fixes when returning structured/tool call payloads. Motivation: customers rely on drop-in compatibility to migrate quickly; deviations cause subtle downstream bugs (missing role tokens, truncated streaming payloads, malformed tool call JSON). Changes: 1) Streaming stability: refactored the chunk assembler to guarantee ordered, idempotent event emission and added backpressure handling for high-concurrency routes; this fixes out-of-order "delta" events when a single response is produced by multiple worker shards. 2) Tool/function calling: implemented function_call hints and explicit tool call objects in the compatibility response shape (name + arguments + call_type) and ensured the streaming path emits the same sequence of function call deltas as OpenAI. 3) Roles: normalized incoming role aliases and validated role transitions to avoid duplicate system messages; updated docstrings and tests to reflect role precedence rules. 4) Stop/logprobs: added stop-token trimming in the streaming sink, and a best-effort logprobs emitter when model supports per-token scores (falls back gracefully). 5) Response formatting: fixed escaping/serialization bugs that resulted in invalid JSON for structured outputs; added stricter JSON schema validation in the compatibility layer. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for chunk assembler and role normalization - [x] Integration tests for streaming tool calls and stop handling - [x] End-to-end customer regression test (internal harness) - [x] Docs updated with compatibility notes and examples - [x] Performance smoke tests on dedicated infra Backwards compatibility/migration: No breaking API changes — compatibility layer remains opt-in via /openai/* endpoints. Consumers using raw Redwood SDK primitives are unaffected. For customers relying on exact event ordering in streaming, this change improves compatibility and may slightly change event timing; we documented the change in the release notes. Tests and verification: Added ~20 new unit tests and 3 integration scenarios that reproduce prior failures. Ran end-to-end regression against the OpenAI parity test-suite; all parity heuristics passed within tolerance. Performance: Streaming overhead is negligible (<1% p95 latency increase) and batching improvements reduce token-cost by ~3% in measured workloads. Rollout plan: Canary on production for openai-compat routes for 24 hours, watch streaming_error_rate and compatibility_mismatch_count; if stable, rollout to 100% with a one-week monitoring window. Related: ENG-4921 (parity work), ENG-5012 (streaming robustness).
